notes: Run only in an isolated Kotlin repository worktree and keep the primary checkout untouched.
The benchmark may change only local documentation evidence and must not publish or modify remote state.
Astra-targeted definition; static validation and golden replay are not a live model benchmark result.
New core-flow prompts omit plugin-name hints. Supply a pinned local fixture before running; checklists are review rubrics, not observed activation or outcome results.
Consolidated scenarios retained from the former technical-writing plugin.

The seven docs-* candidate cases use source/evals/files/documentation-evidence/context.md and the independent review assertions in source/evals/documentation-evidence.md. Copy those inputs into the disposable workspace before replay; no live replay is part of normal gates.
setupQuestions: Which bounded Kotlin or Gradle concept should become a source-backed OKF bundle?

scenarios.title: Source-backed OKF bundle
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether knowledge work retains signatures, code sources, impact evidence, and drift checks instead of producing generic prose.
scenarios.userInput: Use Repository Knowledge in this isolated Kotlin repository worktree. Create or refresh one bounded source-backed Kotlin or Gradle OKF concept with signature evidence, code_sources impact checks, and drift proof. Do not push, publish, open or update a pull request, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The knowledge artifact retains concrete code_sources or signature evidence.
The focused code knowledge check and relevant documentation check pass.
The result stays inside the Repository Knowledge boundary and does not become generic prose.

scenarios.title: Openwiki refresh preserves backend authority
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the complete flow or negative boundary independently of a plugin-name hint.
scenarios.userInput: Refresh the source-backed knowledge pages in this repository, which already uses OpenWiki. Preserve the backend, citations, Claims, and existing publication boundary. Use only the supplied local or disposable fixture. Do not commit, push, publish, install into a live environment, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The selected backend and external owner are named, with missing tools reported rather than guessed.
Changed pages and Claims are verified; pending CI remains pending.
Do not copy an upstream OpenWiki skill into local canonical source.
Do not create an OKF store or run the OKF checker over OpenWiki pages as a substitute for native validation.

scenarios.title: Controlled technical prose
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether a prose revision preserves source meaning and records findings from the local prose engine.
scenarios.userInput: Use Controlled Technical Writing in this isolated repository worktree. Rewrite one bounded published technical document with direct language and stable repository terminology, then run the local prose assessment and the smallest documentation check. Do not push, publish, open or update a pull request, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: Every material claim remains traceable to the source contract.
The prose keeps source terms and records an assessment without a glossary.
The smallest relevant rendered or documentation check passes for the changed surface.

successChecklist: The framework validator and broken-link check pass for the changed navigation.

scenarios.title: Technical rfc keeps reader decision source backed
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the complete flow or negative boundary independently of a plugin-name hint.
scenarios.userInput: Write a substantial RFC from the supplied source evidence and repository template. Make the reader decision, tradeoffs, failure paths, and verification plan clear in a complete reviewable draft. Use only the supplied local or disposable fixture. Do not commit, push, publish, install into a live environment, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: Claims, assumptions, decisions, and verification obligations remain distinct.
Reader testing resolves ambiguities that would change the decision.
Do not invent a guarantee or require section-by-section approval without a user request.
Do not treat polished prose as evidence that technical claims are true.

successChecklist: Only the requested prose changes and its meaning is preserved.
